title: Kefa and Dishes
statementMd:
When Kefa came to the restaurant and sat at a table, the waiter immediately brought him the menu. There were $*n*$ dishes. Kefa knows that he needs exactly $*m*$ dishes. But at that, he doesn't want to order the same dish twice to taste as many dishes as possible.

Kefa knows that the $*i*$-th dish gives him $*a*_{*i*}$ units of satisfaction. But some dishes do not go well together and some dishes go very well together. Kefa set to himself $*k*$ rules of eating food of the following type — if he eats dish $*x*$ exactly before dish $*y*$ (there should be no other dishes between $*x*$ and $*y*$), then his satisfaction level raises by $*c*$.

Of course, our parrot wants to get some maximal possible satisfaction from going to the restaurant. Help him in this hard task!

## Input

The first line of the input contains three space-separated numbers, $*n*$, $*m*$ and $*k*$ ($1 ≤ *m* ≤ *n* ≤ 18$, $0 ≤ *k* ≤ *n* * (*n* - 1)$) — the number of dishes on the menu, the number of portions Kefa needs to eat to get full and the number of eating rules.

The second line contains $*n*$ space-separated numbers $*a*_{*i*}$, ($0 ≤ *a*_{*i*} ≤ 10^{9}$) — the satisfaction he gets from the $*i*$-th dish.

Next $*k*$ lines contain the rules. The $*i*$-th rule is described by the three numbers $*x*_{*i*}$, $*y*_{*i*}$ and $*c*_{*i*}$ ($1 ≤ *x*_{*i*}, *y*_{*i*} ≤ *n*$, $0 ≤ *c*_{*i*} ≤ 10^{9}$). That means that if you eat dish $*x*_{*i*}$ right before dish $*y*_{*i*}$, then the Kefa's satisfaction increases by $*c*_{*i*}$. It is guaranteed that there are no such pairs of indexes $*i*$ and $*j*$ ($1 ≤ *i* < *j* ≤ *k*$), that $*x*_{*i*} = *x*_{*j*}$ and $*y*_{*i*} = *y*_{*j*}$.

## Output

In the single line of the output print the maximum satisfaction that Kefa can get from going to the restaurant.

## Note

In the first sample it is best to first eat the second dish, then the first one. Then we get one unit of satisfaction for each dish and plus one more for the rule.

In the second test the fitting sequences of choice are 4 2 1 or 2 1 4. In both cases we get satisfaction 7 for dishes and also, if we fulfill rule 1, we get an additional satisfaction 5.
statementZhMd:
当 Kefa 来到餐厅并在桌旁坐下时，服务员立刻给他拿来了菜单。菜单上有 $*n*$ 道菜。Kefa 知道自己需要正好吃 $*m*$ 道菜。不过，他不想重复点同一道菜，以便尽可能品尝更多种类的菜肴。

Kefa 知道，第 $*i*$ 道菜能为他带来 $*a*_{*i*}$ 点满足度。但有些菜肴搭配起来并不合适，而有些菜肴搭配起来则非常美味。Kefa 制定了 $*k*$ 条如下类型的进食规则：如果他在吃完菜肴 $*x*$ 后紧接着吃菜肴 $*y*$（$*x*$ 和 $*y*$ 之间不能有其他菜肴），那么他的满足度会增加 $*c*$。

当然，我们的鹦鹉希望从这次餐厅之行中获得尽可能高的满足度。请帮助它完成这个艰巨的任务！

## 输入格式

输入的第一行包含三个用空格分隔的数 $*n*$、$*m*$ 和 $*k*$（$1 ≤ *m* ≤ *n* ≤ 18$，$0 ≤ *k* ≤ *n* * (*n* - 1)$）——菜单上的菜肴数量、Kefa 吃饱所需的菜肴数量，以及进食规则的数量。

第二行包含 $*n*$ 个用空格分隔的数 $*a*_{*i*}$（$0 ≤ *a*_{*i*} ≤ 10^{9}$）——他从第 $*i*$ 道菜中获得的满足度。

接下来的 $*k*$ 行包含各条规则。第 $*i*$ 条规则由三个数 $*x*_{*i*$、$*y*_{*i*$ 和 $*c*_{*i*$ 描述（$1 ≤ *x*_{*i*}$、$*y*_{*i*} ≤ *n*$，$0 ≤ *c*_{*i*} ≤ 10^{9}$）。这表示如果你在吃完菜肴 $*x*_{*i*$ 后立即吃菜肴 $*y*_{*i*$，那么 Kefa 的满足度会增加 $*c*_{*i*$。保证不存在满足以下条件的下标对 $*i*$ 和 $*j*$（$1 ≤ *i* < *j* ≤ *k*$）：$*x*_{*i*$ $=$ $*x*_{*j*$ 且 $*y*_{*i*$ $=$ $*y*_{*j*$。

## 输出格式

在一行中输出 Kefa 从这次餐厅之行中能够获得的最大满足度。

## 说明

在第一个样例中，最好的选择是先吃第二道菜，然后吃第一道菜。这样每道菜可以获得 1 点满足度，并且由于满足了一条规则，还能额外获得 1 点满足度。

在第二个样例中，符合条件的选择顺序为 4 2 1 或 2 1 4。在这两种情况下，菜肴本身带来的满足度都是 7；此外，如果满足规则 1，还能额外获得 5 点满足度。
